Data Production.definition: The national production and the two releases a year, run inside Third Horizon.

truths.label: By Nov 30
truths.text: V11 is delivered to MMA, the last data Handl receives, and NetNav 2.0 launches on it.
truths.measure: MMA confirms receipt of the v11 tables; the 2.0 pilot group reads v11 in January.

big.text: V11 ingestion through delivery (ingestion began October 12; final network list reconciled)
Flagged network plans ingested except Health Payment Systems (no accessible rate data)

truths.label: By the top of the year
truths.text: Third Horizon operates from one unified dataset: a single post-processing source for all production rates and utilization metrics, replacing the separate MMA and Starset National scripts.
truths.measure: Production rates and utilization metrics for MMA and national come from one post-processing run; the MMA-specific reference tables and steerage elements are the only branch.

big.text: Master data table timeline agreed with Park
Codebase updated to run unified post-processing from a single source

truths.label: By May 17
truths.text: v12 is ready May 4 and live May 17 after a two-week test, with the outpatient imputation fix in it.
truths.measure: Data available in the system May 4; 20 to 30 producers used it for two weeks and every flag was resolved or explained; go-live May 17.

big.text: Ingest the March postings (nationals early March, Blues end of March) with the new fields and provider taxonomy
Outpatient imputation variability fixed
Two-week smoke test with 20 to 30 producers, plus the automated variability checks

truths.label: By Oct 18
truths.text: The second release is ready October 5 and live October 18, ahead of the late-year RFP window.
truths.measure: Data available October 5; the test window closed clean; go-live October 18.

big.text: Second national ingestion and post-processing
Two-week smoke test

Data Production.polaris: At the end of 2027, Third Horizon will have delivered high quality market pricing data, on schedule and in a construct that can work with MMA's data delivery system(s).

final.text: Data fidelity stays high and is measured, release by release, so regions first never means data second.
final.measure: Each release passes the shared checklist: data accuracy, reconciliation of the data with the code scripts, release readiness, with named sign-off on both sides.

big.text: QA process drafted for Chicago, November 9: application workflows, data accuracy, release readiness
Shared release checklist with named sign-off agreed with Arindam and Carrie

Regional Engagement.definition: The national paper, market reports, the quarterly town hall, the Raleigh pilot, Thresholds, regional reporting, real-time analytics support.

truths.label: By Nov 30
truths.text: The pilot objective and deliverable are framed before the first client conversation, and we are in conversations with 2 to 3 groups before December.
truths.measure: The pilot process flow exists and carries the capture-rate measurement; 2 to 3 groups are in conversation.

big.text: Pilot process flow drafted, stating the objective of the pilot (we save the client money; the producers think I gotta use this on everything) and carrying the capture-rate measurement (not started as of 10/23)
Screen Third Horizon's own data on each candidate first: Thresholds, Butterball, Grifols, WakeMed (Wake County flagged hard on county procurement)
Thresholds, Chicago: David engages Mark; Peter identifies the producer and account manager
Raleigh candidates under Rick: Butterball, Grifols, WakeMed; producers Todd, William, Brandon

truths.label: Pilots
truths.text: Three pilots run with the producer as the partner and the customer, no friction in their experience, and they suss out the 10 levers.
truths.measure: Capture rate measured in each pilot (the share of identified volume that actually moves); the producer leaves wanting to do it again; a case study after the three.

big.text: The deliverable: the client's data reconstituted through the lens of the 10 levers, with what to do and the vendor or mechanism for each (the mechanism named per lever; MMA owns the strategy and vendor partnerships)
Claim file from MMA's warehouse (Databricks through DataVista); claims stay inside MMA's environment; a region should not see the whole book
Case study after the three pilots
Later: John's context layer in Databricks (producer and analyst expertise), folded into a pilot market; Peter's document ingestion

truths.label: After Pilots
truths.text: The 10 levers are distilled from the pilots into a model, and the national paper applies the general learnings to the national data set.
truths.measure: The model exists as a deliverable of one workstream; the national paper is published publicly and pulls inbound calls.

big.text: Build the 10-levers model as a deliverable of one of the seven workstreams
National paper on the 10 levers (the national number in the billions), published publicly to pull inbound calls

truths.label: Reports
truths.text: Market reports exist for three high-volatility markets, five to 10 pages, AI-templated with human QA, published publicly.
truths.measure: Three reports published; any city can be produced in a week before announcing.

big.text: Build the report so any city can be produced in a week before announcing (Kate)
Choose the three markets; the five upmarket markets flagged: Raleigh, North Texas, Atlanta and Mid Atlantic, Detroit/Troy, Philadelphia

final.text: The regions are engaged on a cadence, regions first and everything else tertiary: a quarterly town hall, stronger regional reporting defined for 2027, and real-time analytics support.
final.measure: Adoption, usage, and leverage tracked by region and by office and driven explicitly; Alex's utilization dashboard is the source.

big.text: Quarterly regional town hall (quarterly for the moment, for cost and the regions' attention)
Stronger regional reporting and back-end usage analytics for the regions, defined differently from the 2026 v10.2 production reporting (Handl's reporting package is a start)
Real-time analytics support: a person a producer can call when they hit a wall mid-analysis
The super user in the chair runs the ten moves proactively on every client rather than waiting to be asked (East with Zibby is the example)
